Die Leistungen umfassen insbesondere die regelmäßige Unterhaltsreinigung der Büro- und Verwaltungsräume, Besprechungs- und Mehrzweckräume, Sanitärbereiche, Teeküchen und Sozialräume, Warte- und Verkehrsbereiche, Treppenhäuser, Aufzüge, Funktionsräume, Lager- und Archivbereiche, Untersuchungs- und Behandlungsräume, Technik- und Versorgungsräume, Werkstätten sowie der Tiefgarage einschließlich der jeweils vorgesehenen Turnusleistungen. Grundreinigungen sowie weitere Regie- und Sonderreinigungsleistungen werden bei Bedarf gesondert durch den Auftraggeber beauftragt. Art, Umfang, Reinigungshäufigkeiten, Qualitätsanforderungen und Ausführungsbedingungen ergeben sich im Einzelnen aus den Vergabeunterlagen, insbesondere der Leistungsbeschreibung und der Kalkulationsdatei einschließlich Einzelraumkalkulation und Flächenverzeichnis.

description: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center - Large Item Scrap Processing and Removal Term Contract IFB No. 2-1-QSC-T-26-112 AMENDMENT (1) NOTIFICATION � AUGUST 26, 2026 Amendment (1) has been issued for IFB No. 2-1-QSC-T-26-112. Prospective bidders are advised that the solicitation package has been revised to address stormwater and environmental permitting requirements, post-bid/pre-award documentation, Performance Guarantee timing, NASA Marshall Space Flight Center environmental coordination, and site access and inspection procedures. Among the revisions, the Apparent Successful Bidder will be required to obtain separate coverage under Alabama Department of Environmental Management (ADEM) General Permit ALG180000 � Salvage/Recycling as a condition of final contract award. Required bidder-controlled post-bid/pre-award actions, including applicable documentation, environmental coordination, permit submission activities, and the Performance Guarantee, are generally required within fifteen (15) business days after written notification that the bidder is the Apparent Successful Bidder, as provided in the amended IFB. Prospective bidders must review Amendment (1), the amended IFB, and all revised solicitation documents in their entirety before submitting a bid. Bidders are responsible for acknowledging Amendment (1) in accordance with the IFB. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) is soliciting sealed bids for a Large Item Scrap Processing and Removal Term Contract for Government-owned DEMIL A scrap located at NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), Huntsville, Alabama. This is a project-driven term contract. Individual scrap processing and removal projects will be assigned to the awarded Contractor through Project Authorizations issued during the contract term. Projects may vary substantially in size, complexity, schedule, location, equipment requirements, and method of execution. Property may include large industrial equipment, aerospace hardware, test articles, pressure vessels, tanks, structural steel assemblies, manufacturing equipment, fabrication scrap, launch vehicle or propulsion-related hardware, obsolete machinery, oversized ferrous and non-ferrous scrap, and other Government-owned scrap designated for disposition. Projects may require dismantling, torch cutting, mechanical size reduction, rigging, crane operations, heavy lifting, loading, transportation preparation, removal, and incidental site cleanup and restoration. Bidders shall submit a single fixed unit purchase price in dollars per pound ($/lb) representing the amount the Contractor will pay the Government for each verified pound of Government-owned property removed under the Contract. IMPORTANT DATES - CENTRAL TIME (CT) IFB Issuance: August 20, 2026 Amendment (1) Issued: August 26, 2026 Deadline for Questions: September 18, 2026 Bid Submission Deadline: September 21, 2026 - 5:00 PM CT Public Bid Opening: September 23, 2026 - 9:00 AM CT Anticipated Pre-Award Date: September 25, 2026 MANDATORY PRE-BID SITE INSPECTION A pre-bid site inspection is mandatory. NASA Marshall Space Flight Center is located within Redstone Arsenal. Prospective bidders must review the IFB and revised Site Access and Inspection Procedures for scheduling and all applicable NASA and Redstone Arsenal access, security, identification, visitor-processing, safety, and inspection requirements. Prospective bidders are encouraged to begin the inspection scheduling and access-approval process as early as possible. Certain access requests, including those involving Lawful Permanent Residents, foreign nationals, or other non-routine access, may require additional processing time and security approval. Failure to obtain required access and complete the mandatory pre-bid site inspection may result in a bid being determined non-responsive. STORMWATER AND ENVIRONMENTAL PERMIT REQUIREMENTS NASA Marshall Space Flight Center operates under National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Permit No. AL0000221. The Contractor will not obtain or modify MSFC's facility permit. As a condition of final contract award, the Apparent Successful Bidder must obtain separate coverage under ADEM General Permit ALG180000 � Salvage/Recycling. Within fifteen (15) business days after written notification that it is the Apparent Successful Bidder, the bidder must complete required bidder-controlled pre-award actions, including coordination with NASA MSFC Environmental, preparation and submission of the applicable Notice of Intent and supporting documentation to ADEM, and provision of evidence of submission to GSA and NASA. The fifteen-business-day requirement applies to actions within the bidder's control. ADEM processing time following a timely and complete submission does not, by itself, make the bidder delinquent. Active ALG180000 coverage is required before final contract award. Refer to the amended IFB and Marshall SWPP Permit Procedures for complete requirements. PERFORMANCE GUARANTEE The Apparent Successful Bidder will be required to furnish a $60,000 Performance Guarantee within fifteen (15) business days after written notification that it is the Apparent Successful Bidder. The Performance Guarantee must be received and approved by the Government before final contract award. Refer to Section 5.2 of the IFB for complete requirements. title: Denmark – Oil spillage monitoring services – Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance
description: This tender concerns a contract for Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance. The overall purpose is to limit and mitigate pollution in the Danish waters — territorial sea and the Danish economic exclusive zone (as defined in the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment (in Danish: Havmiljøloven) section 5) by performing airborne maritime pollution control and to enforce the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment (in Danish: Havmiljøloven). Further information about the characteristics of the airborne maritime pollution control can be obtained from the following sources: — The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea; UNCLOS; — The Bonn-Agreement; — The Helsinki Convention (HELCOM); — The DENGERNETH Plan; — The SWEDENGER Plan; — The Copenhagen Agreement. The supplier enters this agreement with DALO as the contracting party, and the inherent tasks are performed by the Danish Defence. The responsibility for pollution response and counter-pollution surveillance of the marine environement rests with the Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness. As such, this agreement may be subject to transfer to the Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness or an agency under the Ministry's purview, such as the Danish Emergency Management Agency. The maritime pollution surveillance is conducted by airborne area coverage of the Danish waters and this is supplemented by satellite based surveillance by European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA). The Supplier of Airborne Maritime Pollution Surveillance shall overfly areas within the Danish waters — territorial sea and the Danish economic exclusive zone (as defined in the Danish act on Protection of the Marine Environment section 5) two times weekly. The flights shall take place both at day time and at night time and under all weather conditions of common occurrence in the respective areas. Flights will be scheduled by the Supplier. During the flights the Danish waters shall be monitored with the purpose of identifying prospective pollution. Monitoring shall be conducted by means of sensor equipment, which is capable of monitoring the water surface for oil spill etc. The sensor equipment must be made available by the Supplier. During the flights the Supplier shall collect evidence of any observed pollution, hereunder by photo and other documentation and by means of air-drop of oil spill sampling buoys, with the purpose of for example giving the Danish Authorities information to assess the measures to be taken in combating the pollution and providing evidence for further investigation and/or preliminary charges. Specifically the Supplier shall provide the following for airborne maritime pollution surveillance: — Flight system; — sensor equipment; — air crew and system operators necessary for operating flight system and sensor equipment. The Supplier must prior to commencement undertake extensive practical training of his air crew and system operators. The Supplier must ensure that the system operators are at all times duly qualified and trained to perform the task. The Supplier shall be available for participation in multinational operations on behalf of Denmark. The number of such operations is expected to be up to three per year. Participation in such operations is comparable to the flights as described above. The Supplier shall be available/stand by for the duration of these operations.

description: NOTICE TO GOVERNMENT SALES REPRESENTATIVES: The purpose of this amendment is to: 1. Provide site visit attendees from 31 August 2026 2. The site visit is scheduled for 31 August 2026 at 13:00. 3. Change the questions due date from 0800 JST 05 September 2026 to 0800 JST 09 September 2026. 4. Sub-Factor I: Comprehensive design for both playground locations that meets all requirements of this solicitation and SOO, rating table now describes an unacceptable rating as "Proposal does not meet requirements of the solicitation and thus, contains one or more deficiencies." 5. Remove "all sub-factors shall be evaluated on an acceptable/unacceptable basis based on the requirements listed in the SOO and Solicitation" from Amendment to RFO 52.212-1, 2(a) a. Design will be rated on a subjective trade-off basis. 6. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged and in effect. Please review Attachment 12 for full amendment details. ________________________________________________________________________ The 35th Contracting Squadron at Misawa Air Base is seeking qualified vendors capable of providing the design, equipment, and installation of outdoor playgrounds. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, supervision, and other items and services necessary to ensure the install of the outdoor playground is perfromed in accordance with attachment 1 - Statement of Objectives (SOO) Award will be made on a subjective Trade Off basis to the offereor that provides the best value to the USG, in accordance with the Revolutionary Far Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 and 15 in which competing offerors' Technical Capability will be evaluated on basis approximately equal to price. By submission of its offer, the offeror accedes to all solicitation requirements, including terms and conditions, and representations and certifications, in addition to those identified as evaluation factors or subfactors. Failure to meet a solicitation requirement may result in an offer being determined unacceptable. The government reserves the right to award a contract to other than the lowest Total Evaluated Price (TEP). In that event the Contracting Officer will make an integrated assessment best value award decision using the TEP and the Technical Capability rating. Sub-Factor I: Comprehensive design for both playground locations that meets all requirements of this solicitation and SOO Sub-Factor II: Statement of Work conforming to the requirements of the Statement of Objectives, providing the contractor's detailed approach to the installation of this requirement. Sub-Factor 3: Ability to have at least one (1) member of the offerors team present at all meetings and/or site-visits. a. Site visit date is TBD. Amendment to SAM.gov posting will be made with site visit date and time. b. If you require an escorted base pass, please make that request via email to the POCs below no later than 5 days prior to the site visit date. Please reference Attachment 7 - Solicitation - FA520526Q0034, for full evaluation criteria. QUESTIONS All questions are due to the POC below by no later than 0800 JST 05 September 2026 (1900 EST on 06 September 2026) via email. All questions must be submitted in an excel sheet capturing the relevant areas (document, page # & paragraph) the question is in regard to, the question, and any clarification requested. The USG will collect, combine and respond to all questions via amendment to SAM.gov posting. POCs: Shanna.price.2@us.af.mil Kade.forrester.1@us.af.mil

description: NOTICE TO GOVERNMENT SALES REPRESENTATIVES: The purpose of this amendment is to update Playground Reference Maps, add Utility Map for both locations, to provide site visit information, and clarify amendments to RFO 52.212-1 and RFO 52.212-2. 1. Design will be rated on a subjective trade-off basis. 6. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged and in effect. Please review Attachment 12 for full amendment details. ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ The 35th Contracting Squadron at Misawa Air Base is seeking qualified vendors capable of providing the design, equipment, and installation of outdoor playgrounds. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, supervision, and other items and services necessary to ensure the install of the outdoor playground is perfromed in accordance with attachment 1 - Statement of Objectives (SOO) Award will be made on a subjective Trade Off basis to the offereor that provides the best value to the USG, in accordance with the Revolutionary Far Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 and 15 in which competing offerors' Technical Capability will be evaluated on basis approximately equal to price. By submission of its offer, the offeror accedes to all solicitation requirements, including terms and conditions, and representations and certifications, in addition to those identified as evaluation factors or subfactors. Failure to meet a solicitation requirement may result in an offer being determined unacceptable. The government reserves the right to award a contract to other than the lowest Total Evaluated Price (TEP). In that event the Contracting Officer will make an integrated assessment best value award decision using the TEP and the Technical Capability rating. Sub-Factor I: Comprehensive design for both playground locations that meets all requirements of this solicitation and SOO Sub-Factor II: Statement of Work conforming to the requirements of the Statement of Objectives, providing the contractor's detailed approach to the installation of this requirement. Sub-Factor 3: Ability to have at least one (1) member of the offerors team present at all meetings and/or site-visits. a. Site visit date is TBD. Amendment to SAM.gov posting will be made with site visit date and time. b. If you require an escorted base pass, please make that request via email to the POCs below no later than 5 days prior to the site visit date. Please reference Attachment 7 - Solicitation - FA520526Q0034, for full evaluation criteria. QUESTIONS All questions are due to the POC below by no later than 0800 JST 05 September 2026 (1900 EST on 06 September 2026) via email. All questions must be submitted in an excel sheet capturing the relevant areas (document, page # & paragraph) the question is in regard to, the question, and any clarification requested. The USG will collect, combine and respond to all questions via amendment to SAM.gov posting. POCs: Shanna.price.2@us.af.mil Kade.forrester.1@us.af.mil
